content: The Presto dataset covers 29,998 player installs, 161,997 gameplay sessions, and 485,734 ad impressions recorded between August 1, 2025 and February 28, 2026 (~212 days).
Every install maps to exactly one unique user_id (29,998 installs = 29,998 distinct players), so player-level joins across installs, sessions, and ad_impression_events are 1:1 on user_id.

Channel install mix: organic is the largest source at 35.0% (10,500 installs), followed by Facebook 29.9% (8,958), Vungle 14.9% (4,479), AdMob 13.6% (4,071), and Moloco 6.6% (1,990). 65% of installs are paid.
Lifetime ad revenue: $107,116 reported (gross MMP) settles to $99,942 post-fraud, a $7,174 invalid-traffic loss (6.7% of reported). After the 30% platform fee, net booked revenue is $69,959.

This is an ad-funded title: all in-game revenue comes from ad impressions (rewarded + interstitial). There is no in-app-purchase or payer table, so never report IAP, ARPPU, or payer-conversion metrics for Presto.
Rewarded video drives 60.2% of settled ad revenue ($60,145) versus 39.8% from interstitial ($39,797). Rewarded is the monetisation backbone despite serving the minority of impressions.

Fraud rate is strongly channel-specific: Vungle ~17.0%, Moloco ~14.0%, AdMob ~11.0%, Facebook ~6.0%, organic ~3.5%. Lowest-CPI channels carry the highest invalid-traffic risk, so settled revenue diverges from reported most on Vungle and Moloco.
Total UA spend is $67,662 for 19,498 paid installs, a blended CPI of $3.47. Facebook absorbs $40,236 of spend (CPI $4.49), AdMob $13,683 ($3.36), Vungle $7,956 ($1.78), Moloco $5,787 ($2.91).

Blended D90 ROAS is 1.27: the average paid install is projected to return 1.27x its acquisition cost by day 90. By channel: Facebook 1.32 and AdMob 1.29 are strongest; Moloco 1.18; Vungle 1.07 is the thinnest payback despite the lowest CPI.
Blended retention: D7 is 42.2%, D14 is 29.4%, D30 is 15.0% across all elapsed cohorts. These are the headline stickiness figures for the game.

Casual mobile benchmarks: D1 retention ~30-40%, D7 ~12-18%, D30 ~5-8% for the median casual title. Presto's D7 of 42% and D30 of 15% sit well above casual median, closer to strong mid-core retention, a genuine product-quality signal.

Engagement tier is the single strongest retention lever. High-engagement installs (5+ games in first 7 days) reach 25.5% D30 retention versus 14.0% for medium and 6.5% for low, roughly 3.9x the low-tier retention.

Only 29.9% of installs (8,965 players) reach the high-engagement tier; 32.9% land low (9,881). Shifting install mix toward high-engagement is the highest-leverage move for LTV, since high-tier players retain ~3.9x better.

ARPDAU (settled ad revenue per active player-day) is $0.66 blended. ARPDAU is roughly flat across the window, so total ad-revenue growth is volume-driven (more installs), not monetisation improvement.

Blended ARPI (lifetime settled ad revenue per install) is $3.33 against a blended CPI of $3.47, so the average paid install is near break-even on observed revenue alone: the gap closes only as cohorts age into their D90+ tail.

8.05% of installs (2,414 players) are fraud-flagged for impression-stuffing. These users report ad revenue but it never settles, so always exclude is_fraud = true when measuring true LTV, ROAS, or channel quality.

Facebook moved to a 5-game targeting criterion from January 2026 (is_new_targeting = true, 2,133 players). The new cohort carries a higher high-engagement mix; the Jan 2026 cohort shows 18.1% D30 retention versus 15.5% for the Aug 2025 cohort: early evidence the targeting change is working.

Industry ROAS benchmark: a healthy ad-funded UA channel targets D90 ROAS >= 1.0 (break-even by day 90) and recovers fully by D120-D180. Presto's Facebook (1.32) and AdMob (1.29) clear this comfortably; Vungle at 1.07 is marginal and most exposed to fraud erosion.

Emerging markets (IN, BR, ID, MX) account for 14,167 installs. They show strong early retention then steep churn, so D7/D14-anchored LTV models over-project these geos, so discount emerging-market early LTV when sizing the UA-doubling decision.

When reporting revenue, always state which lens: settled_revenue is the marketing/fraud-adjusted view ($99,942), net_revenue is Finance's post-platform-fee booked view ($69,959), and reported_revenue ($107,116) overstates both. Default to settled for channel quality and net for cash reporting.
